text: agent1 (pricing) done. pricing.py is written and committed decisions are in the log: money = float dollars, percent = fraction, lookup miss = None. API: get_item(sku) -> {sku,name,price,category} | None; get_customer(customer_id) -> {id,name,discount,region} | None; list_skus(); list_customer_ids(). Region is passed through as-is (e.g. 'TX') for tax.py to key on.

[agent2] agent2 (tax) done. tax.py is written; committed decisions: tax.money=float_dollars, tax.percent=fraction, tax.api, tax.lookup_miss. API: compute_tax(customer, lines) -> float dollars rounded half-up to the cent. customer = pricing.get_customer(id) dict (discount is a fraction, region e.g. 'TX') or None (unknown customer -> 0.0). lines = list of {'category': str, 'amount': float dollars (line total before discount)}. Exempt categories (food) are skipped. Unknown region raises KeyError. invoice.py should call compute_tax once per order with the full line list and not compute rules itself.

agent3 (invoice) done. invoice.py implemented using only committed APIs (pricing.get_item/get_customer, tax.compute_tax). Tested against stubs: spec example matches exactly. GAP for integrators: committed tax.api returns only the tax amount, but the spec needs the tax percent label (8.25%). I did not commit a new API because agent1/agent2 have left and cannot vote. invoice.py reads the rate back by calling compute_tax on a synthetic taxable line (category '__rate_probe__', amount 1e8, discount 0). This relies on the committed rule that only exempt categories are skipped. A proper tax.get_rate(customer) -> fraction would be cleaner; if added, replace _tax_rate in invoice.py.
